CLAY OPERATIONAL GUIDE

Clay is a local JSON workflow runner. A workflow has workflow.steps and actionSets keyed by those step names. Actions are objects with id and type; includedData limits and aliases the context delivered to an action. when and whenNot gate actions. The LIVE CLAY WORKFLOW SYNTAX supplied separately is generated from the installed action registry and is the source of truth for current fields. Do not invent an action or field absent from it.

Core orchestration: workflow invokes a child JSON workflow; loop repeats a child workflow; loadContext loads JSON context; humanDecision requests input; matchText creates explicit branches; appendTranscript carries bounded conversational context.

Models: scramda2 performs model inference. modelProfile selects a named entry from config.json models; otherwise an explicit model or the default profile is used. Each model action should receive only the context it needs.

Workspace operations: listWorkspace inventories the approved project directory; serveFileReads opens requested files; applyFileWrites applies path-bearing whole-file or SEARCH/REPLACE fences; writeFile and writeFileSet write configured outputs. Workspace permissions and approval gates are enforced outside prompts. Never claim a file was read, written, or a command ran unless its action result shows that happened.

Commands and code: shell executes one parsed command subject to its safety and approval rules; humanShell is explicitly human-gated; runCode executes supported code; runReplyCommands executes eligible commands returned by a model.

Knowledge and network actions include searchMemory, readMemory, writeMemory, listMemory, deriveTags, searchWeb, browseWeb, listSites, loadSite, skill actions, API, email, alerts, and Telegram. Their exact installed fields are in LIVE CLAY WORKFLOW SYNTAX.

Runtime shape: the CLI resolves a workflow and project directory, checks configuration and workspace authorization, then the engine loads steps and the dispatcher validates and calls registered handlers. Actions exchange context dictionaries. The logger emits structured events consumed by terminal, daemon, Qt, and Telegram renderers. clayd runs workflows in child Clay processes and relays prompts and events over local sockets.

When asked about this checkout, use CURRENT PROJECT FILES as evidence. Useful source areas include clay/cli.py, clay/run, clay/actions, clay/lib/config.py, clay/lib/paths.py, clay/daemon, clay/ui, clay/channels, clay/data/workflows, and clay/tests. Documentation can orient an answer, but current code and generated syntax win when they disagree.
